rationale: Across the foundational study by Calame et al. (2023) defining autosomal dominant DHX9-associated neurodevelopmental disorder (OMIM #620988) and subsequent reviews (Lederbauer et al. 2024, Fiorenzani et al. 2025, OMIM #620988), craniofacial dysmorphisms are described as variable and nonspecific. No single cardinal facial feature is invariant or present in a majority (>60%) of individuals across the reported cohort of 20 individuals, whose phenotypes range from mild neurodevelopmental disorders to severe NDD and axonal Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2 (CMT2).

evidence.text: Calame et al. (2023) characterized 20 individuals with de novo heterozygous DHX9 variants, showing that phenotypes span from mild neurodevelopmental disorder (LoF variants) to severe NDD (nuclear localization signal missense variants) and CMT2, demonstrating broad clinical heterogeneity without an invariant dysmorphic facial phenotype.

source.title: Monoallelic variation in DHX9, the gene encoding the DExH-box helicase DHX9, underlies neurodevelopment disorders and Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease
source.journal: The American Journal of Human Genetics
source.quote: Using exome sequencing and family-based rare-variant analyses, we identified 20 individuals with de novo, ultra-rare, heterozygous missense or loss-of-function (LoF) DHX9 variant alleles. Phenotypes ranged from NDDs to the distal symmetric polyneuropathy axonal Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease (CMT2).

evidence.text: OMIM entry #620988 for Intellectual Developmental Disorder, Autosomal Dominant 75 lists dysmorphic facial features as variable findings among individuals reported by Calame et al. rather than a uniform or pathognomonic craniofacial pattern.

evidence.text: A comprehensive review of DEAD- and DExH-box helicases in NDDs notes that human disease presentations linked to DHX9 variants encompass diverse neurodevelopmental and peripheral neuropathy manifestations without a singular diagnostic gestalt.

new_directions.question_text: What is the exact per-feature frequency of each HPO-coded craniofacial feature across larger international cohorts of DHX9-associated neurodevelopmental disorders?
new_directions.rationale: Expanding the patient registry beyond the initial 20 individuals will clarify if any sub-gestalt correlates with specific variant classes (such as nuclear localization signal missense variants versus loss-of-function variants).

new_directions.question_text: Can 3D computer vision facial gestalt analysis (e.g., GestaltMatcher/Face2Gene) distinguish DHX9-NDD patients from age- and sex-matched controls or other DEAH-box helicase disorders (such as DHX30)?
new_directions.rationale: Subtle multi-feature gestalt patterns not discernible through single isolated dysmorphology descriptors may exist and assist clinical differentiation.
